title: Hybrid Connectivity Status

controlTest.positiveScenario: Replay sample `aws:cloudwatch` events with `(  (namespace="AWS/DX" OR namespace="AWS/VPN") (metric_name="ConnectionState" OR metric_name="TunnelState"))` into `index=aws`. Confirm UC-4.4.24 returns >=1 row and the alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign `aws:cloudwatch` traffic without `(  (namespace="AWS/DX" OR namespace="AWS/VPN") (metric_name="ConnectionState" OR metric_name="TunnelState"))`. Confirm UC-4.4.24 returns zero rows and the alert does not fire.

dataSources: `index=aws` sourcetype=`aws:cloudwatch` collected via `Splunk_TA_aws`, `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices`, `Splunk_TA_google-cloudplatform`; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.

description: UC-4.4.24 — Hybrid Connectivity Status: queries multi-cloud (AWS/Azure/GCP) `aws:cloudwatch` for search criteria `( (namespace="AWS/DX" OR namespace="AWS/VPN") (metric_name="ConnectionState" OR metric_nam` and returns actor, resource, and region context for availability review and change validation.
value: On multi-cloud (AWS/Azure/GCP), detecting 'Hybrid Connectivity Status' early shortens cloud incident response and produces defensible audit evidence for identity and change-management controls. UC-4.4.24 drives critical-priority availability alerting before customer-impacting drift.
implementation: Align metric semantics per provider in lookups; alert on sustained unhealthy state. Correlate with provider status pages ingested as `sourcetype=cloud:status`. Dashboard RTO/RPO targets for hybrid links.
visualization: Timeline (link state), Table (circuit, tunnel, status), Map (peering location if geo fields exist).
cimSpl:
| tstats `summariesonly` avg(Performance.cpu_load_percent) as agg_value
  from datamodel=Performance where nodename=Performance.CPU
  by Performance.host span=5m
| sort - agg_value
dataModelAcceleration: Enable data model acceleration for Performance (CPU node).
knownFalsePositives: Short spikes at deploy time, autoscale thrash, or a noisy neighbor on shared hosts can look bad for a few minutes. We require the condition to last across several intervals or clear on its own before we wake someone.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=aws`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_aws`, `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices`, `Splunk_TA_google-cloudplatform` with the modular input for `aws:cloudwatch`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.4.33.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `metric_name` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Align metric semantics per provider in lookups; alert on sustained unhealthy state. Correlate with provider status pages ingested as `sourcetype=cloud:status`. Dashboard RTO/RPO targets for hybrid links.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudwatch" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudwatch" (  (namespace="AWS/DX" OR namespace="AWS/VPN") (metric_name="ConnectionState" OR metric_name="TunnelState"))
| table _time metric_name namespace unit average maximum
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.4.24_hybrid_connectivity_stat_24"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `aws:cloudwatch` in `index=aws` to detect hybrid connectivity status. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the Amazon CloudWatch console Metrics for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `metric_name` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_4_24_alert` with severity aligned to `critical` criticality. Dashboard: Timeline (link state), Table (circuit, tunnel, status), Map (peering location if geo fields exist)..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_aws`, `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices`, `Splunk_TA_google-cloudplatform` and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of hybrid connectivity status so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
